question: Your developer productivity agent summarizes build history for engineers who explore a legacy system. It calls two MCP tools: the CI tool returns build status as numeric codes, and the deployment tool returns status as strings such as "succeeded" and "failed". The agent sometimes reports a failed build as successful because it misreads a numeric code. Which change gives the agent one consistent status format in every case?

options.text: Implement a tool call interception hook that maps the numeric CI status codes to status strings on each outgoing call to the CI tool.
options.reason: Interception hooks act on outgoing tool calls to enforce rules, before any result exists; normalizing returned data is the job of a PostToolUse hook.

options.text: Add few-shot examples to the system prompt that show the agent how each numeric CI status code maps to a status string.
options.reason: Prompt guidance gives only probabilistic compliance, so the agent can still misread a code; the guide prefers hooks when the result must be guaranteed.

options.text: Instruct the agent to run a Bash script that converts each numeric CI status code to a status string before it writes the build summary for the engineer.
options.reason: This still depends on the agent following an instruction, so it is probabilistic, and the agent has already processed the raw result; a PostToolUse hook gives a deterministic guarantee.

options.text: Implement a PostToolUse hook that maps the numeric CI status codes to the same status strings before the agent processes the tool results.
options.reason: A PostToolUse hook transforms tool results deterministically before the model processes them, which is how the guide says to normalize heterogeneous formats such as numeric status codes.
